title: Samson: strength, weakness and grace
share: Set apart from the womb, Samson played with his calling until he lost it. A study of strength, weakness and God’s grace.
opening_question: Samson was set apart to God before he was born, and the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him. Yet he played with his calling until he lost it. What happened, why did it happen, how did God answer his last prayer, and why does Hebrews still name him among the people of faith? Each step asks what happened and what it means for me.

steps.intro: Background first: Israel did evil again, and the LORD delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years (Judges 13:1).
steps.question: What did the angel of the LORD tell Manoah's wife, and what did it mean for the child to be a Nazarite unto God?
steps.apply: What has God set me apart for, and do I treat that calling as holy?

facts.text: "Nazarite" is nazir, from a root meaning to separate. Strong's: "separate that is consecrated".
The vow had three marks: nothing "made of the vine tree", no razor on the head, and no coming near a "dead body".
A Nazarite vow usually lasted a set time, "until the days be fulfilled". Samson was to be one "from the womb to the day of his death".
He would only "begin to deliver Israel out of the hand of the Philistines". The Philistines were subdued later, in the days of Samuel.

steps.question: Why did Samson want the woman of Timnath, what came upon him when the lion roared, and what did he take from the carcase of the lion?
steps.apply: Where do I treat small compromises as harmless because nobody sees them?

facts.text: His parents asked why he would take a wife "of the uncircumcised Philistines". Samson answered: "Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well".
The text adds that "it was of the LORD, that he sought an occasion against the Philistines". God worked even through Samson's choices; the text does not call the choices good.
"came mightily upon him" is tsalach. Strong's: "to push forward". The same words come again when the cords on his arms burn like flax.
A Nazarite was to come at no "dead body". Samson took honey out of "the carcase of the lion", and he told not his parents where it came from.

steps.question: What was Samson's riddle, how did the Philistines get the answer, and what did Samson do then?
steps.apply: How do I react when I feel betrayed or pressured?

facts.text: The riddle: "Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came forth sweetness". Only Samson knew about the lion and the honey.
The companions told his wife: "Entice thy husband". "Entice" is pathah, Strong's: "to open". The lords of the Philistines will say the same word to Delilah.
She wept seven days, and he told her "because she lay sore upon him". Then "his anger was kindled".

steps.question: How did Samson pay the Philistines back, what did the men of Judah do to him, and what did he cry out when he was sore athirst?
steps.apply: Do I turn to God only when I am at the end of my strength?

facts.text: Samson said: "As they did unto me, so have I done unto them". Each side paid the other back, and each time it got worse.
Three thousand men of Judah bound their own judge to hand him over: "Knowest thou not that the Philistines are rulers over us?"
Here, for the first time, Samson "called on the LORD". God gave water, and Samson named the place En-hakkore. Strong's: "fountain of One calling".

steps.question: Why was Samson in Gaza, what did the men of the city plan, and how did he get away?
steps.apply: Do I mistake God's patience for His approval?

facts.text: In Timnath he "saw a woman"; in Gaza he "saw there an harlot". What he saw led him.
He took "the doors of the gate of the city, and the two posts" and carried them up to a hill "before Hebron", far inland and uphill. His strength was still there, but that did not mean all was well.

steps.question: How did Delilah wear Samson down, what did he finally tell her, and what does verse 20 say he did not know?
steps.apply: Where am I playing with a commitment I made to God?

facts.text: Each of the lords of the Philistines promised her "eleven hundred pieces of silver".
Three times he told her lies, and each time men were lying in wait in the chamber. The third answer came close to the truth: "the seven locks of my head".
"she pressed him daily with her words", until "his soul was vexed unto death". Then "he told her all his heart".
"he wist not that the LORD was departed from him". "wist" is yada, to know. The strength had always come when "the Spirit of the LORD came mightily upon him".

steps.question: Look back at Timnath, the lion's carcase, Gaza and Delilah. What pattern do you see, and where does it lead?
steps.apply: What repeated pattern in my life could lead to a fall if I do not deal with it?

facts.text: It begins with seeing and wanting: "I have seen a woman", "Get her for me; for she pleaseth me well", "saw there an harlot", "he loved a woman in the valley of Sorek".
Each time he went a little further: a marriage his parents begged him not to make, honey from a dead lion, a harlot in Gaza, and at last "he told her all his heart".
James describes the same road: "when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death".

steps.question: What did the Philistines do to Samson, where did they put him, and what small sign of hope is in verse 22?
steps.apply: Even in the consequences of my sin, where can I see that God is not finished with me?

facts.text: The eyes that "saw" in Timnath and in Gaza were put out. The man who carried off the gates of Gaza was bound "with fetters of brass" in Gaza and made to grind in the prison house.
"the hair of his head began to grow again". "grow again" is tsamach, Strong's: "to sprout". The text says no more, but it lets us notice.

steps.question: What were the Philistines celebrating, what did Samson ask of God in verse 28, and what happened when the house fell?
steps.apply: What would it look like for me to stop relying on my own strength and depend on God?

facts.text: The Philistines praised Dagon: "Our god hath delivered Samson our enemy into our hand". The question was whose God is God.
The man who had followed his eyes now asked "the lad that held him by the hand" to bring him to the pillars.
"remember me, I pray thee, and strengthen me, I pray thee, only this once": "remember" is zakar and "strengthen" is chazaq. He knew now where the strength came from.
The prayer is honest: he also asks to be "avenged of the Philistines for my two eyes". Yet he calls on the LORD instead of trusting himself, as he did once before when he was "sore athirst".

steps.intro: Closing: Hebrews 11 lists Samson with all his flaws. He is remembered not because he was faithful, but because God is.
steps.question: Where does Hebrews name Samson, who is named with him, and what did they do through faith?
steps.apply: If God could use Samson, what does that mean for my failures?

facts.text: Samson stands with Gedeon, Barak and Jephthae, judges whose stories also show weakness, and with David and Samuel.
"out of weakness were made strong": "weakness" is astheneia, Strong's: "feebleness"; "made strong" is endynamoo, "to empower".
Samson's last prayer was "strengthen me", and Hebrews says they "were made strong". The strength was God's from the start.
